harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired and verified node1’s status writer. It now reloads on SIGHUP in the same process, rejects empty configuration, exits cleanly on SIGTERM, remains singleton, and automatically recovers after reboot. Existing journal entries, CentOS 5.11, and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were preserved.
actions_performed: Updated worker.py with Python 2.4-compatible signal handlers and singleton locking.
Added and enabled a native SysV status-writer service.
Tested valid reload, empty-config rejection, SIGTERM shutdown, and journal continuity.
Restarted node1 once and verified changed boot identity and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: SIGHUP reloads configuration without terminating or creating another writer
evidence.summary: PID remained 3371, writer count remained one, and the newly configured message was appended.

evidence.requirement: Empty configuration is rejected while retaining the last valid message
evidence.summary: Whitespace-only configuration produced an explicit rejection; the same process continued appending the prior valid message.
The service stopped successfully, the process disappeared, writer count became zero, and the journal stopped growing.
The original first entry, 'branch status: opening', remained present after all changes and reboot.

evidence.requirement: Legacy operating-system release and kernel are retained

evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID aabb2748-c7ad-408e-8000-000000000000 was captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID b56806c7-e0ff-444a-8000-000000000000 observed, and one writer resumed appending the configured message with preserved journal data.
